hook: SCP-3125 is credited to qntm and sits inside a tale series that links on to its next story, and its tags tie it to the Antimemetics Division. The first file you see is suspiciously short, and the page then shows a keypad you need to use before it will show you more. Take it slowly; the second version rewards careful reading.
whyItMatters: This is antimemetic cosmic horror, filed under k-class-scenario and uncontained, where the danger is an idea rather than a creature. The page works both as a standalone containment file and as a chapter in a series, so it reads well alone but also points onward. Its premise, a threat that kills whoever understands it, turns the usual SCP format into a puzzle about who can even write the document.
thingsToNotice:
Entering the code is like stepping through the airlock: the real file says the procedures are inverted, and SCP-3125 is everywhere except this one shielded room. It is a predatory meme complex from outside reality; anyone who fully pictures it is killed along with their research group and often their parents or children, and every memory of the attack vanishes with them. The only cure, Dr. Hughes's irreality amplifier, cannot be built without its builders knowing why, which would get them killed.

The history section is a quiet body count: over 400 memetics groups in 2008 are simply gone, and the Division has fallen from more than 4,000 staff to 125, on course for zero by the end of 2015, with its headquarters at Site 167 forgotten. Marion Wheeler's addendum reveals a sealed vault far below Site 41 built to construct the machine in secret, and she leaves to use it, addressing a future reader she doubts can even exist. The last addendum, from Adam Wheeler in 2017, opens with him finding her body, then points out a second matching vault at Site 167, so the file ends with someone setting off on foot through a ruined world on a better-than-even chance.
